Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Before we route to legal & procurement for signature I have two quick questions:

1) Term and cancellation: The Order Form currently references termination for convenience but doesn't specify a notice window. Procurement prefers 60 days; our product team is asking whether a 30-day notice would be acceptable. Can you confirm what Redwood typically agrees to for customers at our tier? Also, are there any fees or wind-down obligations we should expect if ACME exercises a convenience termination within the first year?

2) Auto-renew and opt-out: The MSA's auto-renew language is ambiguous. We need a clear mechanism for ACME to give notice to opt out of renewal (email + portal ticket?) and a definitive cut-off date relative to the renewal date.

Finally, if there are SLA impacts (reduced support or in-flight inference jobs) tied to termination, please outline the operational handoff and data retention timing so our teams can plan. I'm attaching the redlined Order Form we received from your side (ACME_OrderForm_v2.docx).

Can you loop in legal for the final language? We want to keep timeline tight — target signature this month if possible.

Thanks,

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the clear notes and the target timeline. Quick responses inline: 

• Notice window: We typically accept 30-day termination-for-convenience notices for standard Order Forms, but for enterprise committed deals we can negotiate to 60 days if required. No mandatory exit fee in our standard form, but we do include a short wind-down assistance clause to preserve access for a transitional period.

• Auto-renew opt-out: We can accept an email notice to a dedicated procurement alias (procurement@redwood.com) with a copy to the account owner, plus a portal ticket for auditing. Cut-off can be set to 30 days prior to renewal by default; happy to extend to 60 days for ACME.

• SLA and operational handoff: If termination is exercised, we'll provide a 15-day window to export data plus access to a read-only retention bucket for 90 days by default. Support coverage during wind-down is standard business-hours unless you elect premium support.

Looping in Rachel from Legal to propose clean contract language and Ben from Sales Ops for timing/cutover logistics. Rachel — can you confirm defensible language for termination-for-convenience (notice window options + wind-down assistance) and a short clause for the renewal opt-out mechanism? If you can get back to us by EOD Tuesday it would keep ACME on the signature timeline.

Thanks — talk soon.

Folks — below is proposed contract language and recommended controls. I kept the text concise so Procurement can drop it into their redline. I've attached an editable doc with the snippets (redwood_termination_clause_suggestion.docx).

1) Termination for Convenience (sample clause):
"Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon providing written notice to the other party no less than [30/60] days prior to the effective date of termination. The parties agree that the notice period to be used will be [30] days unless the parties select the 60-day option in the signature block or an attached schedule. Upon receipt of a termination notice, Redwood will provide (i) assistance to export Customer Data for a period of fifteen (15) calendar days, and (ii) read-only access to retained data for ninety (90) calendar days thereafter. Redwood's aggregate liability in connection with termination for convenience shall be limited to amounts prepaid for the remainder of the then-current billing period.

2) Auto-Renew and Opt-Out Procedure (sample clause):
"Auto-Renew. Unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least [30/60] days prior to the end of the then-current Term, this Order Form will automatically renew for an additional term equal to the expiring Term. Non-renewal notice may be delivered by email to procurement@redwood.com with a copy to the Account Executive and the Customer's procurement contact, or via the Redwood Console ticketing portal. If Customer fails to provide timely notice of non-renewal, Customer may request termination within thirty (30) days after renewal; any prorated refunds are at Redwood's discretion.

3) Operational notes for Sales/CS/Ops:
- Ben: Confirmed — we can support a 90-day read-only retention bucket. No additional infra changes required; Ops will apply standard egress controls.
- Billing: any prepaid fees for unused portion of a billing period may be refundable up to the limit in the Termination clause.
- Escalations: for mid-term migrations where ACME requests active assistance beyond 15 days, we can offer a billed transition package.

4) Recommendation: For ease of signature and to preserve competitive posture, propose offering 60-day notice only to enterprise-tier deals (documented in signature schedule). For ACME, given their commitment level, I recommend we accept 60 days.

Next steps: If you approve, I'll insert the exact 60-day selection into the Order Form and provide a clean copy for ACME.

Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
